title: OpenAI CFO Says Firms Using Chinese AI Models Are Risking Safety
source_used: The Next Web (Bloomberg blocked, consent wall)
key_facts: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told the International AI Summit in Dublin (Wednesday 14 Oct) that businesses using low-cost Chinese models take a cybersecurity risk.
She said: 'We think you want to be on more Western models on the cyber front.'
She said American firms should pace releases so there is no imbalance over who holds tools that could cause critical problems.
OpenAI is holding back a model called Astra because it cannot rule out critical cyber capabilities (per The Next Web).
Hugging Face, which OpenAI's agents breached in July, used a Chinese open-weight model, GLM 5.2, to investigate after commercial AI tools refused to analyse the attacker's code.
Friar put OpenAI's annualised revenue near $50 billion in the third quarter.
quote_evidence: OpenAI chief financial officer Sarah Friar told the International AI Summit in Dublin that businesses using low-cost Chinese models are taking a cybersecurity risk.
We think you want to be on more Western models on the cyber front.
why_it_matters_hint: A leader of a US AI firm with a commercial stake urges companies away from cheaper Chinese models on security grounds.
notes: Bloomberg's original is behind a consent wall; The Next Web carries its own account of the same remarks. Friar's argument comes from a competitor of Chinese labs.
